entries.title: @three-ws/pumpfun-skills coinFees works again
entries.summary: coinFees() read pump.fun's /coins-v2/<mint> route, which now answers 404 for every coin. It reads the coin record from pump.fun's search route (exact mint match) and reports an unknown mint as coin_not_found. A custom coinsV2Base still reads <base>/<mint> for devnet backends.

entries.title: Coin pages show what each coin actually paid its creator again
entries.summary: pump.fun retired the per-coin timeline the coin page and agent earnings read, and every coin started showing "This coin paid 0 SOL" with a false gap against the wallet total. The per-coin figure now comes from pump.fun's creator-fee index filtered to that one coin, a failed read is shown as unknown instead of zero, and the reconciliation compares the per-coin sum with the wallet total so fees from coins outside the registry show up as a gap.

entries.title: Forge goes by one name everywhere
entries.summary: The text and image to 3D generator is now called Forge across three.ws, and Forge by three.ws inside the tools it plugs into: the Blender add-on, the ComfyUI nodes, the Omniverse extension, the Unity, Godot and Unreal bridges, the Modly extension, the Semantic Kernel, n8n, Raycast and Poe integrations, and the Blender MCP server. Shared Forge model pages now end their titles with "Forge · three.ws", and Forge models carry "Forge by three.ws" as their generator credit in GLB and OpenUSD files. The desktop app keeps its installed name, three.ws Forge.

entries.title: pump.fun skill scripts read coins again
entries.summary: The swap, coin-fees and create-coin skills' fetch-coin script asked pump.fun's retired /coins-v2 route and failed for every coin. It now reads pump.fun's coin search and keeps only the exact mint, so agents can tell a bonding-curve coin from a graduated one before they trade or claim fees.

entries.title: Docs · Incident response
entries.summary: How three.ws detects, contains, communicates and closes a production incident, including a security incident or a personal-data breach, with the code or runbook behind each step.

entries.title: A private agent's profile no longer shows an earnings error
entries.summary: The Earned card on a private agent's profile used to ask for earnings that only the owner may see, then show "Couldn't load earnings" with a Try again button that could never succeed. Visitors now simply do not see the card, the owner still sees their figures, and the retry is kept for real outages.

entries.title: A prompt, a photo, or a video frame becomes a model in the terminal
entries.summary: On /tty, describe an object, drop a photo, or pick a video and the page builds a real model, then draws it in the terminal panel. The same thing works from the shell: three-tty --prompt, three-tty photo.jpg, or three-tty --find, which uses the newest image in the folder. A video contributes one frame, reconstructed as an object. A full walkthrough cloud stays on /capture. Making a model needs a free three.ws account.

entries.title: Agent ideas no longer fail when one model answers in the wrong shape
entries.summary: The Create-Agent "describe it" generator used to take the first answer any model gave, so a model that replied in prose or ran out of room mid-answer ended the request with "unreadable result" even though other models were ready. It now moves on to the next model until one returns a complete agent spec.

entries.title: Agent net worth holds the last known balance while Solana RPC is slow
entries.summary: An agent's net-worth look, and its social card, now fall back to the wallet's last known balance when the Solana RPC lanes are slow to answer, instead of showing an error or an empty card. Only a wallet that has never been read still reports that it is temporarily unavailable.

entries.title: Agent profiles stop requesting a private body they cannot show
entries.summary: When a public agent wears a private avatar, its profile asked for that avatar anyway and was always refused, for every visitor. Both agent profile layouts now skip that request unless you own the agent, so the page loads with one fewer failed call and the owner still sees the body.

entries.title: Agents with a private body load cleanly for visitors
entries.summary: When a public agent wears a 3D body its owner keeps private, its profile, classic view and walking preview now show the default body straight away instead of first requesting the private model and failing. The agent's AR page explains that the body is private and links back to the agent rather than reporting a load error, and the save-avatar card no longer fetches the same avatar twice.

entries.title: An avatar whose model file was deleted now reports not found instead of a server error
entries.summary: When the main storage credential is rejected and neither the backup bucket nor the public storage domain has an avatar's model, the model endpoint now answers 404 not found. It used to answer 502, which told viewers and embeds to keep retrying a file that no longer exists.

entries.title: Avatar thumbnails render again while the storage signing key is refused
entries.summary: The thumbnail backfill read each model through a signed storage link, and while that signing key was refused every render failed and the avatar was retired after three tries. Models are now read through the storage fallback chain, so thumbnails keep filling in, and avatars retired by that outage are put back in the queue automatically.

entries.title: Avatars created during the storage outage load again
entries.summary: While our primary object store refuses its credential, new avatar models are saved to a Google Cloud backup bucket. The avatar model endpoint that the widget, /walk and every embed read never looked there, so those avatars failed to load and showed the robot placeholder instead. It now reads the backup bucket, and pinning such an avatar to IPFS works too.

entries.title: Busy coin charts stay up when the main price source is rate limited
entries.summary: When many visitors open the same coin's chart at once during a market data slowdown, the backup price oracle is now asked once and the answer is shared, instead of every visitor asking separately and some of them getting an error.

entries.title: Chat stops wasting turns on free models that no longer exist
entries.summary: OpenRouter quietly retired eight free model routes, including the Nemotron 3 Super option in the agent, avatar, editor and chat model pickers. Picking it now runs Nemotron 3.5 Super, agents that saved a retired model keep answering on its closest live successor, and the fallback chain and image understanding no longer spend a request on a dead route before reaching one that answers. The nightly free-model audit now watches every route the chain actually calls, so the next retirement is caught the day it happens.

entries.title: Coin cards no longer give up on a live bonding curve when Solana RPC is busy
entries.summary: When every Solana RPC provider was rate limited, the bonding curve read reported live coins as having no curve at all, and the coin cards on /launches stopped refreshing. A busy or unreachable RPC is now treated as a temporary outage: the read tries the next provider, serves the last good figures when it has them, and only a curve that truly does not exist is reported as missing.

entries.title: Coin charts load on every timeframe and ride out data-provider throttling
entries.summary: The 3m, 30m, 2H, 6H, 8H, 3D, 1W and 1M chart timeframes asked our candle provider for groupings it does not offer, so they often showed "Price history is unavailable". They are now built from the nearest supported candles. Charts also fall back to the last good candles from the past day when the provider rate-limits us, instead of failing.

entries.title: Concept images keep a second Hugging Face route, and image health tells the truth
entries.summary: Hugging Face stopped routing FLUX.1-schnell through nscale, so the second Hugging Face rung of the text-to-image ladder failed on every call. It now runs on WaveSpeed, which Hugging Face still maps to the model. /api/v1/ai/image?health=1 now asks each Hugging Face route whether it would actually serve, so an empty credit balance or a retired route shows as down with the reason instead of passing on a valid token. Images made on Hugging Face or the Livepeer network are now credited to that lane instead of to NVIDIA.

entries.title: Crypto Data API token endpoints accept ?mint= as well as ?address=
entries.summary: /api/crypto/holders, /security, /due-diligence and /token now read a token passed as ?mint=, the name /bonding and /whales already use, instead of answering 400 missing_address for a mint the caller plainly sent.

entries.title: Delegation revocations stay indexed on busy chain days
entries.summary: The ERC-7710 delegation indexer skipped every event from delegations three.ws never issued only after paying an RPC call for each one, so a busy block range on the shared DelegationManager outlasted the five-minute cron and replayed forever. It now discards foreign events from the log itself, so revocations and redemptions of your agent's delegations are recorded every tick.

entries.title: Exchange links in a coin's Markets table open the right venue
entries.summary: When a coin page's Markets table is served by a backup data source, each venue now links to its CoinGecko exchange profile, matched by id or name against CoinGecko's own exchange list. A venue with no clear match shows as plain text instead of a link to a page that could not load, and an exchange id that does not exist now answers not found instead of an upstream error.

entries.title: Image understanding says when an image link is the problem
entries.summary: POST /api/vision with an imageUrl that points at a missing file, a host that does not exist, or a web page instead of an image used to run every model in the chain and answer 502 as if the models were down. It now answers 400 invalid_image_url straight away with the reason, and an image served under a generic content type is recognised from its bytes.

entries.title: Large 3D models no longer stop downloading at 20 seconds when storage is slow
entries.summary: While the main storage credential is being replaced, some files are served from the public storage domain, which throttles. A model file larger than a few megabytes that downloaded slowly was cut off exactly 20 seconds in, leaving viewers with a broken model. The download now continues for as long as data keeps arriving and is stopped only if it stalls completely.

entries.title: Long-tail coin pages load during CoinGecko throttling, and Fear & Greed has a working backup
entries.summary: When CoinGecko and CoinPaprika both refuse, a /coin page now falls back to CoinMarketCap instead of showing an error. CoinMarketCap's coin is checked against an independent price reading before it is shown, and only its verified market cap is displayed. The Fear & Greed index backup now reads the CoinMarketCap key production actually holds, so it answers when alternative.me is down.

entries.title: Model and image requests stop paying for a rejected storage credential
entries.summary: While the main storage credential is rejected, every model and image request first made a failing call to it before the backup bucket answered. After one rejection the platform now goes straight to the backup for a minute, then retries the main bucket once so a fixed credential recovers on its own. The storage health check shows when this is active.

entries.title: Models and thumbnails made during the storage outage load everywhere
entries.summary: Every link we hand out for a stored file (Explore cards, fresh upload links, share and wallet-embed previews, pinning, PowerPoint export) now goes through our own /cdn/ address, which serves both the primary store and the Google Cloud backup bucket. Before this, links pointed at the primary store's public domain, so anything saved while that store was refusing our credential answered 404 there.

entries.title: News analysis and AI answers fail less often when traffic spikes
entries.summary: When many readers or a crawler opened the same story at once, every request ran its own article analysis, and those duplicate runs used up the free AI providers for everyone else on the platform. Requests for a story that is already being analyzed now share that one run. The AI fallback chain also stopped skipping a fast model just because a slower model on the same provider timed out, so NVIDIA's quick Nemotron model now gets its turn instead of the request failing.

entries.title: Older avatars and models load faster and stop timing out during the storage outage
entries.summary: Models saved before our main storage provider started refusing us were only reachable through a slow, rate-limited public link, so some avatars and GLBs took over 10 seconds or failed outright. The first time one of them is opened now, a copy is kept in our own Google Cloud bucket, and every later load comes from there.

entries.title: Pages left open across an update reload themselves instead of breaking
entries.summary: A tab opened before a site update could fail the next time it loaded a feature, because the files it asked for had been replaced. Every page now notices when a file it needs is gone, reloads once to pick up the new version, and never reloads in a loop.

entries.title: Photo, scene and model uploads work again during the storage outage
entries.summary: While our primary object store refuses its credential, uploading a reference photo to Forge, a scene, a print file or an avatar model answered "storage unavailable" or failed in the browser. Uploads now go straight to the Google Cloud backup bucket under the same name, and the file is readable everywhere the moment it lands.

entries.title: Price charts load for thinly traded coins during a data outage
entries.summary: When the primary market data source is rate limited, a coin's price chart falls back to a second price oracle. That fallback now looks for the nearest price around each point on the chart instead of only within ten minutes of it, so coins priced every few hours (tokenized stocks, thin tokens) show a full 7 day and 365 day chart instead of an error.

entries.title: Pump.fun bonding curves show the SOL they have really raised
entries.summary: Pump.fun renamed the curve fields that hold a coin's SOL, and some of our readers still asked for the old names. The on-chain curve read behind coin pages and agent alpha failed on every live coin, the pump.fun MCP worker and the stats snapshot reported every live curve as 0 SOL raised, and Strategy Battle paper sells returned almost nothing because the SOL held in the curve was read as lamports. All of them now read the current fields, so curve progress, liquidity and paper-trade results match the chain again.

entries.title: Saved animations play again while object storage refuses its key
entries.summary: Opening or playing a saved animation clip no longer fails with a storage error when the signed storage read is refused: the clip is read from the bucket's public copy, the same fallback avatar models already use. Who may see a private or paid clip is unchanged.

entries.title: Scene Studio loads saved scenes reliably and explains when 3D cannot start
entries.summary: Opening /scene could stop partway through loading when a saved scene asked for its lighting environment before the 3D renderer had finished starting, so models passed in the link and handoff animations never arrived. The environment now waits for the renderer. If WebGPU cannot start, the studio switches to WebGL on its own, and if this browser cannot run 3D at all, the viewport says so and explains how to turn it on instead of staying blank.

entries.title: Solana API endpoints answer a clear 400 for a mistyped address
entries.summary: The Solana endpoints on /api/v1/x (largest holders, token supply, balance, account, token holdings, transaction) now check that an address or signature is valid base58 before asking an RPC node. A typo used to wait about seven seconds and come back as a 502 internal error. Now it answers immediately with a 400 that names the bad parameter.

entries.title: Solana name lookups work again
entries.summary: Looking up a .sol name had stopped working everywhere on the platform after a name-service library upgrade. Paying a .sol name, the /api/sns resolver, agent name tools, showing a wallet's primary .sol name, claiming a <label>.threews.sol subdomain, and checking or registering an agent's .sol domain all work again. When the Solana name service cannot be reached, you now get a clear retry message instead of a false "name not found" or "domain available".

entries.title: Solana reads back off when every RPC lane is rate limited
entries.summary: With Helius at its monthly cap and the free lanes answering 429, each page read re-asked the same exhausted lanes and logged a failure on every request. After one read exhausts the chain on rate limits, other reads now wait a few seconds and are served from the last good answer, so pages keep their data and the providers get room to recover. When every lane is resting, reads now try the one closest to recovering first instead of a paid lane that is out of quota for hours.

entries.title: Stopped code runs say they were stopped
entries.summary: Running code in a sandbox run that you (or the safety guard) had already stopped could answer "backend unavailable" when the machine that run was tied to was offline, which read like a temporary outage worth retrying. A stopped run now always answers that it was stopped and why, and the safety guard checks a run before anything else.

entries.title: Stuck avatar jobs now close with a clear reason instead of retrying forever
entries.summary: About 17 avatar generations stayed in the rigging step for days: their un-rigged model had been saved to the backup bucket while the main bucket was rejecting writes, and the recovery read only looked at the main bucket's URL, so it failed with a 404 every five minutes. Recovery now also reads the backup copy, and a model that is genuinely gone is closed as failed with a message to generate again.

entries.title: The Arena no longer breaks when a network returns a page instead of data
entries.summary: If a proxy or captive portal answered the Arena's data request with a web page, the tournament spotlight threw an error. It now treats that like any other failed load and keeps the rest of the page working.

entries.title: The Hunyuan3D 2.1 GPU worker answers its health check during a cold start
entries.summary: While the worker was still loading its model, its health check crashed on a half-loaded library and answered with a server error, so probes could read a starting backend as a broken one. It now reports the GPU as unknown until loading finishes.

entries.title: The live pump.fun trade stream recovers from socket drops in a fraction of a second
entries.summary: The public Solana lane that feeds coin intel and the sniper's trade stream drops its socket every 10 to 30 seconds. The stream now resubscribes on the same lane within a few hundred milliseconds instead of a full second, so far fewer trades are missed, and a closed stream no longer keeps reconnecting to a lane in the background.

entries.title: The Oracle social feed skips suspended X accounts instead of failing on them every run
entries.summary: A suspended handle in the tracked list was read and logged as a failure on every run of the social ingest. A suspended, deactivated or unavailable account is now reported once and skipped for 24 hours, so the failure log only shows faults worth acting on.

entries.title: The terminal can walk, flock, shade, and splat
entries.summary: curl three.ws/tty/walk plays a person walking in profile. The same stream now has a flock of birds, a lit torus, a raymarched shader, a lathed solid, and a point garden whose banner states the real point count. A parade plays two walks in turn, meet draws both characters in one frame, and say puts your words above the walker. Glyph styles are half-block, braille, density, ASCII, a green matrix tint, and points.

entries.title: The text and image to 3D page now says what it is: Forge, AI 3D Model Generator
entries.summary: The /forge page heading now reads Forge: AI 3D Model Generator instead of a bare Forge, and its browser, search and share titles and description lead with the same words. Someone searching for a free AI 3D model generator can now tell from the result that this is one. It is the same free text and photo to 3D studio, and on narrow screens the heading and tagline wrap cleanly instead of squeezing into a column.

entries.title: The Trenches page keeps showing recent data when the market service is slow
entries.summary: When the live market service stalls, Trenches now shows the last real data it received, labelled with the time it was taken, and keeps refreshing in the background instead of going offline. It only shows the offline panel when no recent data exists at all.

entries.title: Token holder and due-diligence panels load while busy Solana nodes refuse
entries.summary: The top-holders list and the due-diligence report for a Solana token (including $THREE) answered "holder data sources are temporarily unreachable" whenever the first few public Solana nodes in our failover chain turned the request away, even though healthy nodes further down the chain could answer in a fraction of a second. A node that explicitly refuses a request now steps aside without using up the request's retry budget, so the healthy nodes get asked and the panels fill in.

entries.title: Token sentiment pulse reads Bluesky when pump.fun refuses
entries.summary: The sentiment pulse (and the paid sentiment_pulse tool) failed for every coin for five days because pump.fun stopped serving its community callouts to outside callers. It now also reads Bluesky posts that name the coin's mint or its exact $TICKER cashtag, reports each source's status separately, and only answers with an error when every source is down.

entries.title: Unlisted agent profiles stop offering a co-pilot link that cannot open
entries.summary: An agent that is not listed on the marketplace no longer shows visitors an Alpha Co-pilot panel whose link could only fail, and its profile no longer asks for marketplace data that is reserved for the owner. Owners still see both on their own unlisted agents.

entries.title: 360 video and photos now solve into camera positions on our own GPUs
entries.summary: The new pano_sfm stage splits each stitched 360 frame into a rig of flat views and solves where the camera was with COLMAP 4.2.1, so the splat trainer can start from a real 360 walk. Measured on an L4 GPU: a 30 second indoor clip registered every view in 3 minutes, an Insta360 X6 outdoor walk registered all 816 views (0.52 px error), and an Insta360 X5 walking tour registered 85 percent. Footage the solver cannot place now fails with a plain walk-slower message instead of a bad scene.

entries.title: The Android widget token stays on the phone it was linked on
entries.summary: The three.ws Android app no longer copies the home screen widget's sign-in token into Google Drive backups or onto a phone restored from one. A new phone gets its own token when you link the widget from three.ws/glance. Found by a Google Play compliance scan of the 1.1.0 build, which now passes with no critical findings.

entries.title: Docs · Hero clips with Grok Imagine Video
entries.summary: Turn any three.ws model into a short hero clip: the first frame is a real render of the creator's own mesh, six rendered angles guide Grok Imagine Video, presets and tiers, limits, the job API, and the honest no-key state that offers the model's own animated turntable instead of a fake clip.

entries.title: Docs · Paid data and wallet custody for the x402 loop
entries.summary: How the x402 loop keeps the full response of every paid call for accounting and reuse, and how every wallet it creates keeps two sealed key copies, a database that refuses to lose them, and a daily recovery audit.

entries.title: Step Inside Your 360 Photo
entries.summary: Drop one 360 photo, or a raw .insp file, and stand inside it in 3D. Depth estimation builds a metric shell you can look around, step through and download as GLB or PLY. Works with Insta360 X3, X4, X5 and X6 photos, and any 360 camera.

entries.title: Turn 360 Footage into 3D You Own
entries.summary: Walk around with a 360 camera and get a Gaussian splat you can download as PLY or SPZ. Step inside one 360 photo, use it as your avatar's world, or capture motion. Works with Insta360 X3, X4, X5 and X6 files, and any 360 camera.

entries.title: Tutorial: Turn 360 Footage into 3D
entries.summary: How to shoot a 360 walkaround that reconstructs, then turn it into a downloadable Gaussian splat, step inside a single 360 photo, or capture motion, with troubleshooting for every error code. Works with Insta360 X3, X4, X5 and X6 files, and any 360 camera.

entries.title: 360 capture tools on the free studio MCP server
entries.summary: Agents can now turn 360 footage or a 360 photo into a 3D scene over MCP: pano_capture_start, pano_capture_status, pano_capture_list, pano_scene_create and pano_scene_status on /api/mcp-studio (full and Grok surfaces, signed-in accounts). They call the same lanes as the capture pages, so a job started from an agent shows up in the browser. Start tools take a public https URL; local files go through the three-ws CLI.

entries.title: 360 captures train into a real Gaussian splat with a flythrough preview
entries.summary: The pano2splat worker has a splat_train stage: it trains a splat from the reconstructed camera poses, checks quality on held-out frames, and writes a PLY, a compact SPZ and a 20 second 1080p preview video.

entries.title: A 360 photo becomes a metric depth shell
entries.summary: The new model-panodepth GPU worker turns one equirectangular photo into a metric depth shell (GLB, PLY and a depth map) with MoGe-2 (MIT). It was proven end to end on five real 360 photos on an L4 GPU, about 80 seconds each, and every GLB passes the glTF validator with zero errors.

entries.title: A page and tutorial for turning 360 footage into 3D
entries.summary: The new /insta360 page explains how to turn a 360 walkaround into a Gaussian splat you can download as PLY or SPZ, step inside one 360 photo, or capture motion from a 360 clip, with a shooting guide and links to each tool. It works with Insta360 X3, X4, X5 and X6 files, and any 360 camera. A step-by-step tutorial covers each route and every error code.

entries.title: Agents set to Grok Build 0.1 now answer on Grok 4.7
entries.summary: xAI stopped serving Grok Build 0.1 on November 19. The model menus no longer offer it, and any agent, embed or saved setting that picked it now answers on Grok 4.7, the model Grok Build itself runs on, instead of failing. The Grok model check now also reads xAI's release notes, so the next retirement is caught the day it is announced.

entries.title: Click the person in a 360 clip for motion capture
entries.summary: /video-to-motion and /motion-swap now accept a stitched 360 clip from any 360 camera. The page detects the 2:1 frame, opens a sphere preview where you drag to look around and click the person to follow (or let it pick), sends that spot as a yaw and pitch with the capture, and shows what the tracker followed beside the avatar when the worker returns it. Raw .insv files get a clear note to export a 360 MP4 first.

entries.title: Every x402 call the platform pays for is kept, and no loop wallet key can be lost
entries.summary: The platform's own x402 loop now stores the full response of every paid call with its receipt (transaction, paying wallet, amount, endpoint), deduplicated by content and spooled to object storage if the database is briefly unavailable, so the data bought can be reused and every wallet's spend reconciled. Each wallet the loop creates now keeps two independently sealed copies of its key, one under a Cloud KMS key that cannot be exported, the database refuses to delete or re-key a wallet and archives any replaced key copy, and a daily audit proves every key still opens and alerts if one does not.

entries.title: Grok conversations reuse xAI's prompt cache
entries.summary: Every Grok call three.ws makes now tells xAI which conversation it belongs to, so follow-up turns with the same agent reach the server that already holds that agent's persona and tools in its cache. Cached input costs a quarter of the normal rate and starts the reply sooner. Only a one-way fingerprint of the prompt is sent, never the text. The Grok usage report now shows how much of each lane's input came from the cache.

entries.title: Motion capture from 360 video follows the person for you
entries.summary: Send a stitched 360 clip to Video to Motion or Motion Swap and the worker finds the person on the sphere, keeps a perspective camera pointed at them (even across the wrap-around seam), and captures their motion from that view. You get the usual animation plus the reframed video and the camera track it followed, so you can see exactly what was tracked. Optionally pass the direction to the person to skip the search. Regular videos behave exactly as before.

entries.title: Premiere Pro panel for 360 capture
entries.summary: A UXP panel for Adobe Premiere Pro 25.6 or later sends a 360 clip (or the selected sequence clip's in and out range) to three.ws, uploads it in resumable parts, shows live progress with cancel, and imports the preview, poster and scene files into a three.ws captures bin, with one button to insert the preview at the playhead. Source and a built .ccx live in integrations/premiere-uxp; the Adobe Exchange listing is an owner step.

entries.title: Private agents and operator notes stay private
entries.summary: An agent marked private no longer shows up in the public screen stream or the net-worth leaderboard, and a deleted agent disappears from both. Internal operator documents (runbooks, partner pipelines, fundraising material, prompts) are no longer published under /docs, bundled into /docs/ALL.md, or indexed by docs search, and the build now fails if one slips back in. The public x402 status, ring report and fresh-worker feeds keep their numbers but stop echoing raw database errors, upstream RPC URLs and the names of missing signing secrets; operators still see the full detail with their ops credentials.

entries.title: Raw Insta360 files stitch into level 360 video on our own GPUs
entries.summary: The new pano_stitch stage reads the lens calibration and gyro that Insta360 X-series cameras write at the end of every raw .insv and .insp file, so you no longer need an exported file from the camera app. It pairs split X3 files, handles the single-file two-track X5, blends the seam, matches exposure, optionally levels the horizon from the gyro, trims without re-encoding, and writes a 360 video or a photo with the metadata viewers expect. Measured on real X3 and X5 footage: a 5 second X3 clip stitches in 21 seconds on one L4 GPU at 1920 wide and in 49 seconds on 8 CPU cores, and levelling cut the measured tilt of the X3 clip from 3.3 to 1.5 degrees.

entries.title: Resumable uploads for multi-gigabyte 360 capture files
entries.summary: The new /api/capture-upload endpoints (create, sign, parts, complete, abort) upload 360 videos, photos and raw .insv, .insp and .lrv files up to 8 GiB straight to storage in parallel parts. A dropped connection costs one part, and a resumed upload re-sends only what is missing. Limits are 3 uploads in progress and 32 GiB per account per day. A 2.19 GB file killed mid-upload and resumed came back byte-identical.

entries.title: Send 360 footage from Blender and get the splat back in your scene
entries.summary: The three.ws Blender extension (version 1.1.0) has a new 360 Capture panel. Pick a 360 video, either a 2:1 equirectangular mp4 or the raw .insv file from an Insta360 X3, X4, X5 or X6 camera, and it uploads in resumable parallel parts, becomes a 3D Gaussian splat on three.ws, and lands in your scene selected. A single 360 photo, including a raw .insp, comes back as a depth shell mesh instead. With the KIRI Engine 3DGS Render add-on enabled the splat renders as Gaussians; without it you get a coloured point cloud. Choose a quality preset, trim the clip, pick the up axis, cancel at any point, and reopen past captures from the Your captures list, with the preview video one click away in the sequencer. Blender stays smooth while a job runs, and the panel respects Allow Online Access.

entries.title: Start a 360 scene from a link when uploads are down
entries.summary: The /pano-scene page now takes a public https link to a 360 photo or .insp as well as a file. While our file storage is recovering, an upload says so plainly and offers that link box instead of failing on a broken request, and /api/scene-upload answers 503 storage_unavailable with retry-after so other clients can do the same. When the 3D server refuses a photo, you now see its reason instead of a bare status code, and the progress shows the Mesh step while the shell is being built.

entries.title: Step inside your 360 photo
entries.summary: The new /pano-scene page turns one 360 photo, or a raw .insp file, into a 3D shell in real metres. Drop it, watch the real stages (stitch, depth, mesh), then look around, step off-centre and use your phone's gyroscope inside it, or download the GLB and PLY. Works with Insta360 X3, X4, X5 and X6 photos, and any 360 camera.

entries.title: Turn 360 footage into a 3D scene on /capture
entries.summary: A new 360 video tab on /capture previews your footage on a sphere right in the browser, lets you trim it, and uploads big files in resumable parts you can pick up after a reload. Then it shows the scene being built step by step and hands you a viewer, a preview clip, and SPZ and PLY downloads. Works with any 360 camera.

entries.title: Upload 360 footage and start a scene from the terminal
entries.summary: The three-ws CLI gains a capture command: three-ws capture 360 <file> uploads a 360 clip, stills set or .insv from any 360 camera in resumable 8 MiB parts and starts the reconstruction, capture scene <photo> turns one 360 photo into a scene, and capture status, list and cancel follow the job. An interrupted upload picks up where it stopped. It signs in with a stored login or THREE_WS_API_KEY. /openapi.json now documents every capture upload, pano-capture and pano-scene route with request and response schemas, the error shape and examples taken from real responses.

entries.title: Use your own 360 photo as your avatar's world
entries.summary: Drop an equirectangular photo from any 360 camera on the viewer, or paste a link, and it becomes both the light on your avatar and the backdrop behind it. Lighting and background are separate switches with rotation, blur and brightness sliders, and a brighten-highlights option makes a clipped sun light the avatar like a real one. Huge photos are resized safely on phones, a non-360 image or a blocked link explains itself, and the same backdrop control is on the Splat Viewer. Embeds accept it through the environment attribute.

entries.title: Your 360 scenes keep building after you close the tab
entries.summary: A 360 capture is now saved to your account the moment you start it. It keeps processing with the tab closed, the finished scene is copied into our own storage so its links never expire, and every capture shows on My creations under 360 scenes: finished ones open in the splat viewer, unfinished ones reopen their progress view, and failed ones offer Capture again. You can cancel a capture that is still running or delete a finished one with its files, and up to two can process at once. Developers get the same through /api/pano-capture.

entries.title: Docs · Grok Voice realtime on a lip-synced avatar
entries.summary: How /voice/grok and the grok-realtime embed attribute talk to a 3D avatar through xAI's speech-to-speech model: the server-side session broker, lip sync delayed to match your speakers, measured reply and mouth latency, the honest fallback without a key, and the LiveKit and Pipecat examples.

entries.title: Docs · Share to X and Ask @grok
entries.summary: The Share on X and Ask @grok actions on every model, avatar and anatomy page: X's weighted length rule, the UTM tags, the click counters and the large image card each page unfurls.

entries.title: Talk to a 3D avatar with Grok voice
entries.summary: Speech to speech with a lip-synced 3D avatar: pick an avatar, hold to talk or leave the mic open, and watch the measured reply and mouth latency for every turn.

entries.title: Ask @grok about any model, avatar or machine, straight from its page
entries.summary: Every 3D model, avatar and anatomy cutaway now has two X actions in its share menu: Share on X, and Ask @grok about it, which posts the link with one line about the thing and a question for Grok to answer in the replies. The model page's Share button now opens that full menu instead of only copying the link. Posts are fitted to X's real length rule, so a long title or a Japanese or Chinese prompt is trimmed before X can refuse it, and the link is never cut. Every link unfurls as a large card showing the model, avatar or machine itself. On a browser without 3D graphics, an anatomy page now shows a still drawing of the machine instead of an error, and sharing still works.

entries.title: Every three.ws tool and integration asks for an account before it makes a model
entries.summary: The account requirement for making or uploading a 3D model now reaches every place that can do it, and everything that described it is accurate. The Material Studio restyle and colorway tools, GLB uploads in /play, the PowerPoint add-in and Pipeline Studio ask you to sign in, and Microsoft Teams generates on behalf of the signed-in user. The SDKs and plugins (create-agent, the AI SDK and LangChain tools, Google ADK, Dify, n8n, Raycast, Semantic Kernel for Python and .NET, the MCP server package, the 3D AR Studio and its MCP server) send your API key, and Hermes, Cursor, Grok Build, Copilot and ChatGPT sign in with OAuth. A missing or refused key gets a clear message linking to the API keys page instead of a bare error. The cookbook, the docs, the agent card and the partner pages stop promising text to 3D with no account. Browsing, inspecting and viewing models still need none.

entries.title: Four Grok Bot task templates you can paste as they stand
entries.summary: The Grok page now has four ready task templates for Grok Bot: a home-office scene kit pulled from the free catalog, a weekly game-jam prop pack that only generates what the catalog is missing, a product photo turned into a 3D model and checked from two angles, and a rigged mascot avatar with a pose studio link. Each card has a one-click copy of the exact prompt, the tools it calls, what it returns and how long it took when we ran it against production, from 3 seconds for the catalog kit to about 7.5 minutes for the rigged mascot. The Grok Bot guide gains the same templates, how to share one as a Grok Bot template link, and a step-by-step test path for anyone reviewing the connector: create a free account, then three asks that finished in under a second, about three minutes and about fifteen seconds.

entries.title: Free text to 3D tells the truth about its lane and its wait
entries.summary: The free text to 3D draft lane now says which engine really runs your job (Microsoft TRELLIS on NVIDIA NIM when available, otherwise our own GPU worker) in the API, the MCP server instructions and the docs. The time estimate for a cold GPU worker now reflects the measured boot of several minutes instead of under a minute, and the docs no longer promise a 240 second inline wait: a job on our own GPU returns a queued handle within seconds, so poll it.

entries.title: Hunyuan3D textured models load again
entries.summary: A dependency security update made the Hunyuan3D 2.1 texture stage refuse to load its own bundled paint pipeline, so every Hunyuan3D job failed before it started. The worker now explicitly trusts that pipeline, which ships inside the image, and the build fails if the fix ever stops applying.

entries.title: Live uptime numbers for the Grok MCP connectors
entries.summary: Every five minutes a synthetic client now connects to the Grok-facing MCP connectors exactly the way Grok and Cursor do: it opens a session, lists the tools, makes one read-only tool call and checks the OAuth sign-in challenge, timing every step. The results appear on the status page under Connector uptime, with 24 hour, 7 day and 30 day success rates and how long a connector waits for the tool list, and the same numbers are published as a public feed at /api/status/mcp. A connector that fails twice in a row alerts the team.

entries.title: Making or uploading a 3D model now needs a free account
entries.summary: Anyone could generate a 3D model or upload a photo with no account behind it, and the result landed on a public three.ws link with nobody answerable for it. Generating from text, a photo or a sketch (the free lane included), uploading, refining, rigging and the other creation tools now ask you to sign in first. Forge asks the moment you press Generate or add a photo, so you never wait on a job that cannot start, and every other page shows a sign-in bar with a link straight back. What you make is saved to your account and stays unlisted until you publish it, and only a signed-in owner can make a model public. Browsing, viewing and sharing models still need no account, and the free lane is still free. Scripts, plugins and AI connectors (Blender, ComfyUI, Modly, Omniverse, the Hugging Face Space, the MCP servers and the custom GPT) sign in or send an API key from your dashboard.

entries.title: Manage or report any 3D model from its page
entries.summary: If you made a model, its page now lets you choose who sees it (public, unlisted or private) and delete it for good, even after switching browsers, because the site keeps a private key for every model you make. A private model still opens for you so you can publish it again. Anyone else can use Request removal on the page to report their own lost model, a copyright problem, their likeness or harmful content, and a person reviews every request.

entries.title: Model review moved off the website, and flagged evidence cannot be deleted by accident
entries.summary: The internal review boards for held 3D models and for the Forge quality judge are gone from the public server: there is no admin page or admin endpoint left that can approve, label or delete a model. Operators review from their own workstation with signed-in command line tools instead (npm run forge:safety and npm run forge:judge). The takedown tool now refuses to delete any model the safety screen flagged as possible child abuse material until the legal report has been filed and recorded, so the evidence is preserved.

entries.title: New 3D models start unlisted until you publish them
entries.summary: A model made from a text prompt used to go straight into the public gallery, feeds, search and sitemaps. Every new model you make now starts unlisted: your link works and you can share it, but it stays out of the public showcase until you choose to make it public on the model page. Uploads from your own photo already worked this way.

entries.title: Paid-call caps and Fastify gating now hold, and the embed docs point at what works
entries.summary: The x402 buyer MCP now enforces the per-call spend cap (MAX_PAY_USD or max_usd) in session-token mode too, refusing before the platform wallet pays. The x402 merchant package now returns a real 402 on Fastify 5 routes instead of serving the paid output, and its README shows the working form. Package repository links point at their real repos, the MCP server README states its free-tool count exactly, and the embed docs load the hosted agent-3d module instead of telling readers to npm install a stale three.ws package.

entries.title: PiXal3D image builds can ship their attention kernels
entries.summary: The PiXal3D worker compiles its neighborhood attention kernels from source, but the build image had no CMake, so every rebuild since the kernel fix failed and production kept the older image without those kernels. CMake is now installed before the kernel build, and a test keeps it there.

entries.title: Public models are safety-checked before they are listed
entries.summary: Before a model appears in the public gallery, feeds, search or sitemaps, its prompt, its preview render and every photo it was made from are screened. Clean models publish automatically; if the screen cannot answer, the model stays unlisted and is retried, then reviewed by a person. Unsafe models are kept private. Three reports for harmful content or someone's likeness also take a model out of public view for review. Nothing you generate is refused, and your own link keeps working.

entries.title: Rocket engine and launch stack cutaways, narrated by Grok
entries.summary: Anatomy now opens with two featured cutaways. The first is a full-flow staged-combustion rocket engine: both preburners and turbopumps spin, six propellant flows are coloured by species, the methane cools the nozzle on its way to the preburner, and the plume shows shock diamonds. The second is a fully reusable two-stage launch system, toured from liftoff through hot staging and boostback to the tower catch. Every number on screen is listed with its public source and date on a Sources page, and anything that could not be sourced was cut. Press Listen in the tour to hear each step. The narration is built for Grok to write from that step's sourced facts only, and the page reads the written step text whenever Grok is not connected. Shared links unfurl as cards rendered from the real cutaway.

entries.title: Signing in to the free 3D Studio connector works in MCP clients
entries.summary: Making a model on the free 3D Studio MCP server (/api/mcp-studio) needs a free three.ws account, but its sign-in pointed MCP clients at the wrong protected resource, so clients built on the MCP SDK stopped before the sign-in page with "Protected resource does not match expected". The studio is now its own OAuth resource: its sign-in challenge, its protected-resource metadata and the tokens the authorization server mints all name /api/mcp-studio, so connectors such as Grok Bot and IBM Bob reach consent and come back signed in. Existing platform tokens keep working.

entries.title: Six runnable examples for building 3D with Grok
entries.summary: A new examples pack shows Grok and three.ws working together six ways: Python with xai-sdk, Node with the Responses API, a single curl script, Grok's X search turning a trending topic into a 3D prop (it drafts a post and never posts), a talking 3D avatar with Grok as its brain, and a walk-through of the three.ws plugin for Grok Build that ends with the model loaded in a three.js starter. Every example has a README with the exact run command, output captured from a real run and what a run costs, and a no-key mode that runs the three.ws side live. One command, npm run grok:examples-smoke, sets each one up in a fresh folder and runs them all against production; the fastest goes from a fresh copy to a finished GLB in about two minutes.

entries.title: Talk to a 3D avatar with Grok voice, speech to speech
entries.summary: A new page at /voice/grok lets you talk to a 3D avatar through Grok Voice, xAI's speech-to-speech model. Your voice goes up and the spoken reply comes back over one connection instead of three separate steps, the avatar's lips move with the reply as you hear it, and you can talk over it to cut in. Every turn shows how long the reply took to start and how quickly the mouth followed. Any three.ws embed can switch its mic button to Grok Voice with one attribute, voice-provider="grok-realtime". The mouth waits for your speakers instead of running ahead of the sound, Bluetooth included. The LiveKit and Pipecat plugins gained Grok Voice examples and fixes so the avatar keeps the first words of a reply and the visitor's own words. Grok Voice needs a free three.ws account, and the page uses the standard voice chain whenever Grok Voice is not available.

entries.title: The /glass lens gets past "Location needed"
entries.summary: The site-wide permissions policy blocked location, compass sensors and the microphone on every page, so the smart-glasses lens at /glass stopped on its first screen for every visitor. /glass now grants exactly those three to itself (the camera stays off, and no other page changes), so the lens can find where you are, which way you face, and hear your reply.

entries.title: The free NVIDIA image step accepts requests again
entries.summary: When you make a 3D model from text, the first step draws a reference picture, and the free NVIDIA FLUX service is the first place it asks. That service changed its rules and began refusing any request that carried a random seed, so every attempt was turned away in under a second and the job had to wait for a backup service instead. Requests no longer carry the seed, so the free step can answer again whenever NVIDIA has capacity.

entries.title: The Hunyuan3D-2 image-to-3D lane loads again, and fails fast when it cannot
entries.summary: The Hunyuan3D-2 worker, a backup lane for photo-to-3D, had stopped loading its texture model after a dependency upgrade: newer diffusers refused its bundled paint pipeline, and newer transformers refused its weights on the older torch it ran. It now trusts its own pinned pipeline and runs torch 2.6 on CUDA 12.4, so the lane generates textured models again. Separately, a job that arrived while either Hunyuan worker was still loading used to wait 15 minutes and report a timeout when the load failed; it now fails at once with the real reason, so the forge moves to the next lane straight away.

entries.title: The three.ws plugin for Cursor gets /make-3d, /rig and /embed
entries.summary: The Cursor plugin now has three commands. /make-3d checks the free catalog, generates a textured model, renders it so the agent can see whether it matches, and prints the GLB, a viewer link, the run receipt and paste-ready embed code. /rig turns a humanoid GLB into an animation-ready one, and /embed writes HTML for any website. Signing in from Cursor now always asks for the same four permissions (read and update your 3D models, see your name and email, stay connected) and nothing else, even when Cursor registers without naming them. The plugin ships a five-minute test plan with measured timings, and the privacy policy now spells out what the plugin's server can reach, how long models are kept, and that prompts and models are never used for training or sold.

entries.title: The three.ws plugin for Grok Build gets /make-3d, /rig, /embed and an art director agent
entries.summary: The three.ws plugin for Grok Build, xAI's coding agent, now does the whole 3D job from the terminal. /make-3d checks the free catalog first and otherwise generates a textured model, /rig turns a humanoid GLB into an animation-ready avatar, /embed writes paste-ready HTML for any model, and /three-ws-init teaches a project's AGENTS.md how to load and embed GLBs safely. A 3d-art-director agent makes a model to a brief, renders it from four sides, fixes the one thing that is wrong and stops after two rounds. Catalog search, render checks and embed code are free with no account; making or rigging a model needs a free three.ws account, signed in once from Grok Build with OAuth or with an API key. The plugin installs in under a second and is ready for xAI's plugin marketplace.

entries.title: three-ws setup offers sign-in for the Grok and free studio connectors again
entries.summary: The directory now describes the Grok and free 3D Studio servers as "none to connect, a free account to make a model", and the CLI read that as no-sign-in-possible, so npx three-ws setup --client grok-bot only offered anonymous and install-token connections and refused --auth key or oauth. It now offers all four ways to connect on both servers, and its server lists stop calling the studio "no account needed".

entries.title: three.ws joins xAI's Grok for Startups program
entries.summary: three.ws has been admitted to Grok for Startups, xAI's program for startups building on Grok, with credits across the Grok API, Grok and Grok Build. xAI now has a card on /partners and /partners/benefits and a place in the site footer's partner row. The credits fund the Grok brain lane agents can think on and sit behind the three.ws Grok connector, which gives Grok Bot, Grok connectors and the xAI API a free 3D studio.

entries.title: TripoSG photo-to-3D stops failing at the background cutout
entries.summary: TripoSG cuts the subject out of your photo with our background-removal service before building the mesh. That service finished the cutout after answering the request, and Cloud Run gave it almost no CPU between requests, so a 20-second cutout dragged past the two minutes TripoSG waits. Its model was also downloaded on first use, and two cutouts at once could run it out of memory. The service now keeps its CPU, ships the model in its image, and has twice the memory, so photo-to-3D on TripoSG completes again. The segmentation service had the same CPU gap and is fixed too.

entries.title: xAI credit ledger with burn-rate and expiry alerts
entries.summary: Every platform-key call to xAI now records tokens and cost, so a new report and an advisory health check show where the Grok credits go and warn before they run out or expire unused.

entries.title: A busy multi-view lane asks you to retry instead of quietly downgrading your model
entries.summary: When the Pixal3D multi-view lane was at capacity, Forge silently handed the job to single-view TRELLIS, which ignored the extra angles you uploaded. Forge now tells you the lane is busy and to retry in about 30 seconds, instead of switching lanes behind your back.

entries.title: Image to 3D from a reference photo works again
entries.summary: Since our object storage credential was rejected, uploaded reference images were saved to the backup bucket but the GPU lanes were still sent the old storage address, which answered 404. For most of today, nearly every image-to-3D request failed with "input image unusable". Reference images now reach TRELLIS and TripoSG through three.ws/cdn, which serves from whichever bucket holds the file, and generations from a photo complete again.

entries.title: The x402 VS Code extension shows real $THREE prices
entries.summary: Endpoints priced in $THREE showed Infinity in the payment summary and the confirm prompt. Amounts now use the token's declared decimals, so you see the actual price, for example 10.000000 $THREE, before you approve a payment.

entries.title: Two-factor setup and sign-in challenges stop returning 404
entries.summary: Enrolling an authenticator app and answering a two-factor challenge called /api/auth/mfa/..., a path production had no route for, so both failed with Not Found. The route now reaches the MFA handler, so you can turn on two-factor protection and sign in with it.

entries.title: A failed free text-to-3D job now says so in minutes, not 45
entries.summary: When NVIDIA's hosted TRELLIS lane errors, its status endpoint answers 410 Gone. We treated that as a job still in progress, so every errored generation sat at "generating" until the 45-minute cleanup. A 410 now goes down the expired-request path: we check whether the model already landed, retry once, and otherwise fail honestly so the request moves to the next lane.

entries.title: A Solana RPC burst limit no longer benches the paid lane for six hours
entries.summary: Token due diligence, holder lists and agent net worth stopped returning 503 during traffic bursts. Our primary Solana RPC answers a short burst limit with the same message it uses for a spent plan, and two bursts in a row used to park it for six hours while it was serving fine. Repeat bursts now widen the retry window gradually, up to one hour, so the paid lane comes back within minutes.

entries.title: The NVIDIA Brev GPU quickstart ships a patched JupyterLab and upload parser
entries.summary: The Brev quickstart image now runs JupyterLab 4.6.5 and python-multipart 0.0.33 behind FastAPI 0.162. That closes the JupyterLab extension-manager, CommandLinker and XSS advisories and the python-multipart file-write, denial-of-service and parameter-smuggling advisories published this year. The studio's image upload, sample picker and resolution checks behave exactly as before.

entries.title: Admin consent (Microsoft Entra)
entries.summary: What the three.ws sign-in app asks for in plain language, and the tenant-wide admin consent link for a Microsoft Entra administrator, with clear success and error results.

entries.title: Docs · Agent chat guardrails (NemoGuard)
entries.summary: Owner opt-in checks on an agent's chat: jailbreak detection, content safety on the visitor's message and the streamed reply, and topic control with a polite redirect. The flow, budgets, fail-open posture, block counts and the owner API.

entries.title: Docs · Call three.ws agents from Copilot Studio and Foundry over A2A
entries.summary: Add the three.ws A2A agent in Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry: endpoint, agent card, API key and OAuth setup, streaming, cancel, and an Agent Framework client sample.

entries.title: Docs · Microsoft Entra SSO and user provisioning
entries.summary: Connect three.ws to a Microsoft Entra tenant: OpenID Connect single sign-on, launch from My Apps, and automatic user provisioning and deprovisioning over SCIM 2.0.

entries.title: Docs · Microsoft IT admin deployment guide
entries.summary: Roll three.ws out to every seat: Teams setup policy, Edge WebAppInstallForceList and ExtensionInstallForcelist through Intune or Group Policy, tenant-wide admin consent, verification, rollback and FAQ.

entries.title: Docs · Omniverse Kit extension
entries.summary: The threews.forge Kit extension: generate a textured model from a prompt or image and reference it into the open USD stage upright and to scale, or import a saved model from your three.ws library. Install, API key handling, import details and the measured GPU test run.

entries.title: Docs · OneDrive and SharePoint in Forge
entries.summary: Pick source photos from OneDrive or SharePoint in Forge and save finished 3D models back to your Microsoft files.

entries.title: Docs · OpenUSD export (simulation-ready)
entries.summary: Export a Forge model or any public GLB as validated OpenUSD for NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim: convex collision hulls, a rigid body with mass from volume times density, semantic labels and skeletons, from the Forge menu, the API or the MCP tool.

entries.title: Docs · Phi brain lane (self-hosted Phi-4-mini)
entries.summary: Microsoft Phi-4-mini self-hosted on a Cloud Run L4: the vLLM worker, tool calling, fallback, measured cold start, latency, throughput and cost, and the 91-task evaluation that sets its routing.

entries.title: Docs · Sharing and link previews
entries.summary: Share creations and agents to Teams and LinkedIn, the link-preview rules both enforce, and how to refresh a stale LinkedIn card.

entries.title: Docs · Talking-avatar clips (Make a clip)
entries.summary: Turn an avatar and a line of text, or an uploaded recording, into a shareable MP4 of that avatar saying it: NVIDIA Magpie voice, Audio2Face-3D lip sync, rendered and encoded in your browser.

entries.title: Docs · The /enterprise procurement page
entries.summary: How the three.ws enterprise page is built: purchase paths, identity, security answers, Microsoft surface statuses from data, the printable procurement packet and the contact form that files a lead.

entries.title: Docs · three.ws 3D for SharePoint and Viva Connections
entries.summary: Admin and site-owner guide for the SharePoint Framework solution: upload the package, allow one script source, then add the Agent web part, the 3D Model web part or the Viva Connections Agent card.

entries.title: Docs · three.ws 3D Studio agent for Microsoft 365 Copilot
entries.summary: The three.ws declarative agent for Microsoft 365 Copilot: what users see, its six conversation starters, how it is validated, sideloading in a developer tenant, and production proof for every starter.

entries.title: Docs · Usage feed for Power BI and Excel
entries.summary: The three.ws OData v4 usage feed: MCP tool calls, LLM tokens and cost, Forge generations and billing for you or your team, read-only keys, query options, paging, limits, and typed Power Query scripts for Power BI and Excel.

entries.title: Enterprise: buy and review three.ws
entries.summary: Buy three.ws for your company through Microsoft Marketplace or by invoice, and clear vendor review in one visit: Microsoft sign-in, Entra tenant claim, SCIM, hosting, encryption, subprocessors and a printable procurement packet.

entries.title: NVIDIA lane benchmarks
entries.summary: Measured health and latency for every NVIDIA lane three.ws runs: NIM chat, vision, embeddings, NemoGuard, Magpie TTS, Audio2Face-3D, hosted TRELLIS and the self-hosted L4 and RTX PRO 6000 GPU workers. 7 and 30 day tables from real probes and real jobs, with a CSV download.

entries.title: Agent memory and knowledge search find the right passage more often
entries.summary: Agent memories, agent knowledge bases and site-widget knowledge now embed with NVIDIA's nemotron-3.5-embed-8b. On our labelled docs set it ranks the right passage in the top five every time (up from 92%) and raises nDCG@10 from 81.3 to 91.3, with gains on two public benchmarks as well. Existing vectors move over in place after the deploy, with no gap in search (a re-embed run refuses to start until production can read the new space), and the old ones are kept until the new space is verified on production data.

entries.title: Agent owners can turn on chat guardrails
entries.summary: Edit agent > Brain > Guardrails lets an owner switch on, per agent, jailbreak detection, content safety on the visitor's message and on the agent's streamed reply, and topic control that politely redirects off-topic questions to the topics the owner lists. Everything is off by default. The checks run on NVIDIA NemoGuard models alongside the reply, so a clean turn barely waits, and the panel shows how many turns each check stopped over 30 days without storing any message text. In our eval, jailbreak detection caught 95% of jailbreak prompts and flagged none of 350 ordinary ones. Agents on the NVIDIA chat lane also no longer return empty or cut-off replies.

entries.title: Agents read the tables, charts and scanned pages in your PDFs
entries.summary: A PDF added to an agent's Knowledge tab is now read page by page with NVIDIA NeMo Retriever models, so tables keep their rows and columns, charts are turned into values, and scanned pages and pasted screenshots of tables are read with OCR. The panel shows each page as it is read and previews the tables it finds, and a View tables button shows every extracted table. On a test of 44 questions over three research papers and a scanned copy, agents answered 90.9% correctly, up from 38.6%. If the models are unavailable, the file is still read as plain text. Arrives with the next deploy.

entries.title: Analyze your three.ws usage in Power BI and Excel
entries.summary: Settings now has a Connect to Power BI or Excel panel. Create a read-only key for your own usage or for a team you own, paste the feed URL into Power BI or Excel, and report on MCP tool calls, LLM tokens and cost, Forge 3D generations and metered billing. It is a standard OData feed, so the Power BI Service refreshes it on a schedule without a gateway, and filters you set in Power Query are applied on the server. Keys can be revoked at any time, every key creation and refresh is in your audit log, and typed Power Query scripts with a starter report are in the repository.

entries.title: Approve or deny your agents' actions from a Microsoft Teams card
entries.summary: When an agent asks to move money or run an action you hold for review, the request now also arrives in your 1:1 chat with the three.ws app in Microsoft Teams. The card shows the agent, the action, the amounts, the destination and the deadline, with Approve and Deny buttons, and it updates to show who decided and what happened. Only the account owner, matched through their linked Microsoft sign-in, can decide; anyone else sees a card with no details. A press goes through the same check as the web inbox, so an altered button, an expired request or a double click never runs an action twice. Turn it on or off and send a labelled test card that runs nothing from the Microsoft Teams panel on /approvals, or type approvals in the chat to list what is waiting.

entries.title: Ask Microsoft 365 Copilot for a 3D model with the three.ws 3D Studio agent
entries.summary: The three.ws Microsoft 365 app now includes a Copilot agent. Pick three.ws 3D Studio in Microsoft 365 Copilot or Copilot in Teams and ask for a product model for a deck, a rigged mascot, a free ready-made asset, paste-ready embed code for a website, or a look at a model from every side. It uses the free three.ws studio tools, so there is no account to create. A generation gives you a viewer link at once that opens the model the moment it is ready, then the GLB download, the poster and how to drop it into PowerPoint.

entries.title: Buying three.ws for a company now takes one page
entries.summary: The new enterprise page gives a company buyer and their security team everything in one visit: how to buy through Microsoft Marketplace or by invoice and purchase order, Sign in with Microsoft, Entra tenant claim and SCIM provisioning, hosting, encryption, retention, every subprocessor, which Microsoft surfaces are live today, and what support is offered. Every status is read from data and states what is true now, so nothing claims a certification three.ws does not hold. A print button turns the page into a procurement packet for vendor review, and the contact form reaches the team directly. Pricing now has a Buying for a company row that leads here.

entries.title: Call three.ws agents from Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry over A2A
entries.summary: The three.ws A2A endpoint now streams over SSE, lets you cancel a running generation, and accepts an X-API-Key header or OAuth 2.0 as well as bearer tokens, all declared in the agent card. Responses are checked against the A2A schema in the test suite, and a builder guide covers adding three.ws in Copilot Studio and Foundry plus a Microsoft Agent Framework sample.

entries.title: Cosmos worlds now render on Cosmos 3 Nano and can grow out of your avatar's own scene
entries.summary: The /cosmos world lane is back. Worlds now render on NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Nano on our own GPU worker, with the older hosted models kept behind it as fallbacks. A new mode picker adds From my scene: the page captures your avatar as it stands on the stage and the world is built from it, as a still that becomes the first frame, or as a depth or edge render of a slow orbit that steers the layout. Progress shows the real step count and time left, and a job survives a reload or a closed tab, so you can leave and come back to a finished world.

entries.title: Every NVIDIA lane, live on /nvidia
entries.summary: The /nvidia page now shows whether each NVIDIA lane we run (NIM chat, vision and embeddings, NemoGuard, Riva speech, Audio2Face and the TRELLIS, Hunyuan3D, TripoSG and Pixal3D GPU workers) answered its most recent scheduled probe, with median and p95 latency over 7 days. A new /nvidia/benchmarks page publishes the full probe, job and GPU fleet tables, measured from real generation jobs, with a CSV download and the method behind every number. The first full run caught a retired NVIDIA model still pinned in the chat chain, which now leads with Nemotron Ultra.

entries.title: Export any Forge model as simulation-ready OpenUSD
entries.summary: Forge models now export as OpenUSD that drops straight into NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim with physics already set up. Pick OpenUSD (simulation-ready) in the Forge export menu and you get .usdz, .usd with textures and .usda: convex collision hulls, a rigid body whose mass comes from the hull volume and a density for the object class, a friction and restitution material, semantic class labels for synthetic-data annotators, and skeletons for rigged avatars. Every file passes the OpenUSD usdchecker and the NVIDIA asset validator before you see it, and a report lists the mass method and every finding. Developers get the same export from POST /api/forge/export-usd and the export_openusd MCP tool.

entries.title: Forge reads photos from and saves models to OneDrive and SharePoint
entries.summary: In Forge image mode, From OneDrive or SharePoint opens Microsoft's file picker so you can bring in up to six photos from a personal or work OneDrive or a SharePoint library, and Save to OneDrive in the Download menu writes the GLB, a poster image and, for a stored model, a one-slide PowerPoint deck into the folder you choose. Microsoft sign-in is asked for on that click only, existing files are never overwritten, large uploads resume after throttling, and closing the picker simply cancels. The buttons appear once the three.ws Microsoft app is connected on the server.

entries.title: Forge results and agent 3D bodies load again
entries.summary: Storage's old public download domain stopped serving files, so some forge results opened to a blank viewer with a broken Download button, and many agents in the directory, the Teams tab and search showed no 3D body. Every one of those links now goes through three.ws's own file proxy, which serves the same files reliably. Older links saved before the change are rewritten when they are read, so nothing has to be regenerated.

entries.title: Generate Forge models straight into NVIDIA Omniverse with the three.ws Kit extension
entries.summary: The new threews.forge extension adds a Forge panel to any Kit 110 app such as USD Composer. Type a prompt or pick a reference image, press Generate, and the textured model is referenced into the open USD stage upright and to scale, at the world origin, the selected prim or in front of the camera, with live progress and cancel. A My models browser imports anything saved in your three.ws account. On an NVIDIA L4 a real image to 3D job went from Generate to framed in the stage in 78.5 seconds, and all 62 extension tests passed with no Kit errors. Install steps are in the extension's README.

entries.title: Get a Teams notification when your 3D model finishes or an agent needs you
entries.summary: Link your three.ws account to Microsoft Teams by sending the bot a one-time code, and finished or failed 3D models, mentions, messages and (if you choose) agent task reports appear in your Teams activity feed and on your phone. Each event has its own switch in Settings, Notifications, with a button that sends a real test notification. Tapping a notification opens the three.ws tab on that model or agent. Uninstalling the app removes the link. A tenant admin approves notifications once with the TeamsActivity.Send permission, and settings shows the consent link if that is still missing.

entries.title: Image understanding now picks the best NVIDIA Nemotron model for each job
entries.summary: Every feature that reads an image (photo checks before 3D generation, the forge quality gate, avatar alt text, scene object boxes, photo to diorama, and the image review behind X mentions) now asks the Nemotron vision model that scored best on that exact job in a measured test of 162 real tasks. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL leads overall, Bolt E4B handles the quality gate and avatar review, and Nemotron 3 Nano Omni writes alt text, each with the others behind it as fallback. A bug that turned the seed judge's scores into text when it repaired a reply is fixed, and photo to diorama now reports which model read your photo.

entries.title: Microsoft community gallery samples
entries.summary: Three ready-to-submit samples for the Microsoft PnP galleries: a Copilot declarative agent, a Teams message extension with link unfurl and a SharePoint 3D viewer web part, each built to its gallery's rules and checked against production.

entries.title: Microsoft Marketplace free trials, from activation to the first paid month
entries.summary: Plans bought on Microsoft Marketplace can now start with a free trial. The activation page says when the trial ends and what it becomes afterwards, using the price Microsoft publishes for the plan. While the trial runs, a slim banner under the site header shows the days left, what it converts to and a Manage in Microsoft link, and you can dismiss it for the session. You get one notification and one email a week before the trial ends and again the day before, never more. Microsoft bills nothing until the trial is over, and cancelling in Microsoft before then means no charge.

entries.title: Microsoft Marketplace subscriptions keep their access through plan and seat changes
entries.summary: We ran the full Microsoft Marketplace subscription lifecycle against Microsoft's SaaS API emulator and fixed what it caught. When a Microsoft-billed subscription moves to a per-seat plan, the buyer who owns it now keeps their access instead of dropping to the free plan. Usage that Microsoft already counted is now recorded as settled when it is sent again, instead of staying pending, and webhook replies now follow Microsoft's documented contract, so a plan three.ws does not sell is refused cleanly. Developers can rerun the same check locally with one command.

entries.title: Microsoft Phi joins the self-hosted model fleet
entries.summary: Microsoft's open Phi-4-mini model is built and tested on three.ws's own GPU fleet, with streaming and tool calling, ready to switch on as a brain an agent can pick by name. We tested it against the current default on 91 real platform tasks and published the results: it trails on every one, so it does not take over any internal work by default yet. If the Phi lane is slow or down, requests move to the next model automatically.
